summary: Padma Subrahmanyam is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Stella Maris College, Ethiraj College for Women, and Annamalai University (~1972–1979) under research supervisor T. N. Ramachandran (~1970–1979).

Padmanabh S. Jaini was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a Professor (attested 1977–1990, 2002) and later Professor Emeritus (attested 2016) at the University of California, Berkeley.

Padmaprasad Upadhyaya Bhattarai is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Vamacharana Bhattacharya and held a post at Rajkiya Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Kathmandu (attested 1957).

Palmira Brummett specializes in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at the University of Chicago and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, later serving at the University of Tennessee (~1989–2011) and Brown University (2011–2016).
Palmo Kyi is a Tibetology scholar. She studied under teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal, as well as supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012).

Pamela D. Winfield works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).
Pamela Gutman was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University (~1972–1976).

Pandurang Vaman Kane was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He held posts at Elphinstone College, Wilson College, Government Law College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).
Pankaj Tandon is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray and held a post at Boston University (attested 2015).

Paolo Visigalli is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome, University of Padua, and University of Cambridge. He held posts at NYU Shanghai (~2017–2021) and Shanghai Normal University (~2022).

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was Director of the Mithila Institute (~1955–1961) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1961–1972), succeeding Shripad Krishna Belvalkar in 1961.

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied as a doctoral student at the University of Chicago (attested 2026) and held a postdoctoral researcher post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Parimal G. Patil specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1994–2002), he became a Professor at Harvard University (~2001).

Parul Dave-Mukherji is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history/archaeology. She earned her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1988–1991) and served as a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2020).

Pascale Haag specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1997–2002) and Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre University (~2014–2018), and held a post at the EHESS (~2003).

Pascale Hugon works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania and held a professorship at Thammasat University (attested 2012).
Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Bristol and at the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012).

Patricia Berger works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, served as Curator of Chinese Art at the Asian Art Museum, and held posts at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Patricia Buckley Ebrey is a historian and Sinologist. She earned degrees from the University of Chicago and Columbia University, later holding faculty posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, the Institute for Advanced Study (1998), and the University of Washington (1997–2020).
